<p class="section-kicker">THE GUIDING QUESTION</p>

## How do we model a physical system well enough to understand, simulate, and control it?

The scale changes—from rigid bodies to flexible structures, from analytical equations to learned representations—but the question stays the same.
:::

::: {.topic-grid}
::: {.topic-card}
<span class="topic-index">01</span>

### Dynamics

Rigid bodies, Kane's equations, reference frames, and multibody systems.
:::

::: {.topic-card}
<span class="topic-index">02</span>

### Flexible Structures

Beam theory, vibration modes, continuum mechanics, and finite elements.
:::

::: {.topic-card}
<span class="topic-index">03</span>

### Control

GNC, pointing manoeuvres, vibration suppression, and input shaping.
:::

::: {.topic-card}
<span class="topic-index">04</span>

### Computational Methods

SymPy, Simscape, numerical models, and reduced-order modelling.
:::

::: {.topic-card}
<span class="topic-index">05</span>

### Physical AI

Learned dynamics, world models, simulation, and intelligent control.
:::
:::
